PMID:39429992.topic: Hip fracture early mobilisation and physiotherapy
PMID:39429992.setting: Queen Elizabeth The Queen Mother Hospital, Margate, Kent; main orthopaedic ward and outlier wards
PMID:39429992.standard: National guidelines (NICE): mobilisation on the day of or the day after hip fracture surgery; two hours of physiotherapy in the first week after surgery; no target stated

cycle1.result: 93% (106/113) seen by a physiotherapist on the day of or day after surgery (main orthopaedic ward 94%, 80/85; outliers 93%, 21/28; P=0.3). 40% (46/113) had delayed mobilisation. 83% (94/113) had two hours of physiotherapy in the first week. Clear documentation of mobilisation in 85% (97/113).

PMID:39429992.other_findings: Reasons for delayed mobilisation: post-operative delirium 32.6% (15/46), low haemoglobin 26% (12/46), pain 21.7% (10/46), dementia 4.3% (2/46), no documented reason 15.2% (7/46). Presence of one or more of these factors was associated with one-year mortality of 25.8% (16/62, P=0.05), with delirium the strongest single factor (P=0.01).

PMID:35860148.topic: Neurovascular assessment documentation in limb fractures
PMID:35860148.setting: Tertiary care hospital / major trauma centre; emergency department and orthopaedic clerking of patients admitted to trauma wards with acute fractures
PMID:35860148.standard: British Orthopaedic Association Standards for Trauma (BOAST) on documentation of neurovascular assessment; no target stated

cycle1.result: ED notes: no neurovascular documentation 17 (22.1%), 'NVI' only 30 (38.9%), specific documentation 30 (38.9%). Orthopaedic notes: no documentation 3 (3.8%), NVI only 16 (20.7%), specific documentation 58 (75.3%). Post-manipulation in ED (n=19): no documentation 12 (63.2%), specific 6 (31.6%).

PMID:35860148.intervention: Posters in trauma units, generic educational emails to all ED and orthopaedic doctors, and consultant-led joint ED and orthopaedic teaching sessions.

cycle2.result: ED notes: no documentation 6 (7.3%), NVI only 8 (9.7%), specific documentation 68 (82.9%). Orthopaedic notes: no documentation 0 (0%), NVI only 4 (3.6%), specific documentation 74 (90.2%). Post-manipulation in ED (n=22): no documentation 7 (31.8%), NVI only 4 (18.1%), specific 11 (50%).

PMID:35860148.other_findings: Post-manipulation neurovascular documentation remained poor, with nearly a third of manipulated patients still having none. Patients clerked by the project authors were excluded from the re-audit.

PMID:36561096.topic: VTE prophylaxis after ankle fracture surgery
PMID:36561096.setting: Sandwell and West Birmingham NHS Trust, single centre, operatively managed ankle fractures
PMID:36561096.standard: NICE guidance on pharmacological VTE prophylaxis for ankle surgery with immobilisation, and BOAST requirement that VTE prophylaxis follows agreed local protocols; no target stated

cycle1.result: Operation note documentation of VTE chemoprophylaxis: agent and duration specified 40 (29%), nonspecific 40 (29%), none 57 (42%). Discharged with VTE chemoprophylaxis 78 (57%).

PMID:36561096.intervention: Quality Improvement Half-Day educating surgeons and ward junior doctors; new written local policy of enoxaparin 40 mg once daily for 6 weeks for all operatively managed ankle fractures unless contraindicated; posters for 3 weeks in theatre and ward areas; review of prophylaxis at 2- and 6-week clinics.

cycle2.result: Operation note agent and duration specified 44 (90%), nonspecific 3 (6%), none 2 (4%) (all P<0.001). Discharged with VTE chemoprophylaxis 48 (98%) (P<0.001).

PMID:36561096.other_findings: In cycle 1, discharge prophylaxis was 97.2% when agent and duration were in the operation note versus 51.8% with nonspecific and 32.4% with no documentation (P<0.001). Two VTE events (one DVT, one PE) occurred in cycle 1 and none in cycle 2.

PMID:39720771.setting: University teaching hospital and regional trauma and orthopaedic referral centre serving four peripheral sites (Our Lady of Lourdes Hospital, Drogheda, per affiliation); non-operative fracture pathway
PMID:39720771.standard: Three modified BOASTs: early senior review (BOAST: new fracture clinic within 72 hours; measured as VFC review within 24 hours), minimising outpatient visits, and patient-initiated follow-up as the default; no target stated

cycle1.result: 39% of non-operative patients triaged to the VFC within 24 hours; 61% sent directly to face-to-face clinic. 35,399 face-to-face fracture clinic appointments (also given as 35,339 in the results).

PMID:39720771.intervention: COVID-19-era policy changes: mandatory VFC triage of all non-operative injuries via a smartphone referral app with daily consultant-led multidisciplinary review, and an early appropriate discharge / patient-initiated follow-up policy; national lockdowns also occurred.

cycle2.result: 100% of non-operative patients assessed in the VFC within 24 hours. Face-to-face appointments fell to 17,639, a 50.2% reduction: 3.7% attributed to national lockdowns, 14.7% to VFC triage and 35.5% to early appropriate discharge.

PMID:39720771.other_findings: Sample sizes are total orthopaedic referrals in each period. Patient safety and satisfaction were not assessed.

PMID:38274927.topic: Elective cancellations due to asymptomatic bacteriuria
PMID:38274927.setting: Lister Hospital, Stevenage (East & North Herts NHS Trust), large district general hospital offering tertiary orthopaedic services; cancelled elective orthopaedic operations

cycle1.result: Of 33 all-cause cancellations, 7 (21.2%) were cancelled for UTI risk on positive urinalysis; only 1 (14.3%) of these was symptomatic, so 6 (85.7%) were cancelled for asymptomatic bacteriuria.

PMID:38274927.intervention: New symptom-based protocol from 1 May 2019: all patients complete a 7-item UTI symptom questionnaire and surgery is cancelled only if two or more symptoms are reported, regardless of urinalysis.

cycle2.result: Of 45 all-cause cancellations, 2 (4.4%) were cancelled for UTI risk, both symptomatic; 4 (8.8%) had positive urinalysis, the 2 asymptomatic ones cancelled for unrelated reasons. No cancellations for asymptomatic bacteriuria; estimated 71.4% reduction in cancellations for UTI risk.

PMID:38274927.other_findings: Patients with positive urinalysis whose operations were not cancelled were not captured, so the true effect is estimated. Each cancelled operation was estimated to waste 2.1 hours of theatre time (about £2,525).

PMID:38903340.setting: Galway University Hospital, orthopaedic outpatient clinic letters
PMID:38903340.standard: Laterality (left or right) stated in the diagnosis in outpatient clinic letters; no named guideline or target stated

cycle1.dates: One week within February to August 2023
cycle1.result: Laterality mentioned in 65.1% of letters. By grade: SHO 78.8%, registrar 62.7%, consultant 54.3% (P<0.05).

PMID:38903340.intervention: Educational sessions on specifying laterality, reminder stickers placed in the clinic as visual prompts, and liaison with secretarial staff who transcribe dictated letters.
PMID:38903340.other_findings: Consultants had the lowest rate of stating laterality at baseline. Re-audit analysed the same number of letters over one week.

PMID:41306811.topic: Hip fracture analgesia and fascia iliaca block in ED
PMID:41306811.setting: Emergency department, Macclesfield District General Hospital
PMID:41306811.standard: NICE CG124 and RCEM guidance: FICB performed where applicable (100%); contraindications documented if FICB not performed (100%); pain re-evaluation within 30 minutes of analgesia (100%)

cycle1.result: FICB performed 26/40 (65%); contraindications documented in 0/14 (0%) without FICB; pain re-evaluation within 30 min 21 (52.5%); mean time to first analgesia 130 ± 28.8 min; mean time to FICB 228 ± 36.2 min.

PMID:41306811.intervention: Practical sessions to familiarise ED clinicians with FICB, and a mandatory analgesia checklist for all suspected neck of femur fractures (pain scores, analgesia times, FICB details and reason if not given).

cycle2.result: FICB performed 26/40 (65%, p=0.74); contraindications documented in 9/14 (64.3%); pain re-evaluation within 30 min 20 (50%, p=0.99); mean time to first analgesia 38.8 ± 13.2 min (p<0.001); mean time to FICB 63.4 ± 19.1 min (p=0.002).

PMID:41306811.other_findings: FICB uptake and pain re-evaluation did not improve despite faster analgesia. No FICB-related complications in either cycle.

PMID:35141091.setting: Non-specialist admitting district hospital (Warrington and Halton Teaching Hospital, per affiliation); emergency department and trauma and orthopaedics, referring to a tertiary spinal centre
PMID:35141091.standard: Local standard operating procedure for acute back pain with suspected cauda equina syndrome, based on BASS/SBNS guidance (senior ED discussion, anal tone and perianal sensation documented, MRI within 24 hours, spinal centre plan documented); no target stated

cycle1.result: ED assessment and senior discussion 24 (96%); discussion with spinal centre by senior ED doctor 13 (61.9%); anal tone documented 23 (92%); perianal sensation documented 18 (72%); spinal centre plan documented per SOP 5 (20%); MRI within 24 hours 25 (100%).

PMID:35141091.intervention: Teaching on CES and neurological examination for T&O and ED juniors, posters of the pathway in ED, discussion between T&O and ED on GP referrals, and emails to staff; an electronic SBAR documentation template was also created.

cycle2.result: ED assessment and senior discussion 26 (90%, p=0.727); discussion by senior ED doctor 2 (9%, p=0.000); anal tone documented 28 (97%, p=0.887); perianal sensation documented 28 (97%, p=0.028); spinal centre plan documented 0 (0%, p=0.033); MRI within 24 hours 29 (100%).

PMID:35141091.other_findings: Referral by a senior ED doctor and documentation of the spinal centre plan worsened, which the authors linked to COVID-19 staffing pressures. Discussion with the spinal centre, post-MRI discussion and management per advice stayed at 100%.

PMID:40995306.topic: Weight-bearing after periprosthetic femoral fracture surgery
PMID:40995306.setting: Dorset County Hospital, district general hospital trauma and orthopaedics; data from the Hip Fracture Registry
PMID:40995306.standard: British Hip Society guidance: aim for full weight-bearing in the immediate postoperative period; no target stated

cycle1.result: 28 (73.7%) had surgery (19 ORIF, 9 revision). Of these, 22 (78.6%) were full weight-bearing, 4 (14.3%) limited weight-bearing and 2 (7.2%) non-weight-bearing. One fixation failure (3.5%).

PMID:40995306.intervention: Results presented at a local orthopaedic educational meeting on aiming for immediate full weight-bearing; no re-audit reported.
PMID:40995306.other_findings: Limited and non-weight-bearing instructions often lacked specific functional restrictions and duration, making rehabilitation difficult. The single fixation failure occurred in a patient allowed full weight-bearing.

PMID:24967296.topic: DVT diagnostic pathway (D-dimer and Wells score)
PMID:24967296.setting: Royal London Hospital, nurse-led Fast Response Team outpatient clinic for suspected lower limb DVT
PMID:24967296.standard: Modified Wells rule (low Wells score with negative D-dimer to avoid ultrasound); re-audit against the local revised diagnostic algorithm; no target stated

cycle1.result: 510 (96.9%) had D-dimer and ultrasound results; 265 (51.9%) negative D-dimer, of whom 143 (53.9%) had a low Wells score. 7 of 143 with negative D-dimer and low Wells score had a DVT, all with a risk factor not in the Wells score; none without risk factors had a DVT (NPV 100%).

PMID:24967296.intervention: Revised clinical diagnostic algorithm adding assessment of extra risk factors to the Wells score; ultrasound omitted in patients with negative D-dimer, low Wells score and no risk factors.

cycle2.result: All 290 (100%) had complete results; 94 (32.4%) negative D-dimer, 43 with low Wells score, of whom 30 had risk factors and were scanned. 1/94 (1%) with negative D-dimer had a DVT (on OCP). 13 of 290 (4.5%) not scanned under the algorithm; all negative D-dimer patients had probability score and risk factors recorded.

PMID:24967296.other_findings: The D-dimer assay changed between cycles, lowering the proportion of negative results. The re-audit saved £767.

PMID:39677174.setting: Queen's Hospital, Burton upon Trent; emergency department and fracture clinic
PMID:39677174.standard: NICE guidance for children's distal radius buckle fractures: removable splint instead of full cast and no routine follow-up; no target stated

cycle1.result: ED: 0% splint (all back slab). Fracture clinic: 62 (95.4%) full cast, 3 (4.6%) splint. Discharged at first visit 5 (7.7%); second visit 56 (86.2%); third visit 4 (6.2%).

PMID:39677174.intervention: New ED and fracture clinic pathway (splint or soft cast with information leaflet and no follow-up), posters in ED and fracture clinic, and email reminders to staff.

cycle2.result: ED: 17 (19.5%) splint, 70 (80.4%) back slab. Fracture clinic: 44 (50.6%) converted to splint and 2 remained in splint (53%), 41 (47.1%) cast. Discharged at first visit 39 (44.8%); second visit 48 (55.2%).

PMID:39677174.other_findings: Discharge at first visit remained suboptimal. Some casts were used because of limited splint sizes, patient preference or lack of technicians at weekends.

PMID:23725485.setting: Department of Orthopaedics, University Hospital Tuebingen

cycle1.result: Mean HVA 36.4 degrees preoperatively, 3.5 at 2 days and 13.4 at 6 weeks (p<0.001); mean IMA 16.8, 6.4 and 9.8 degrees (p<0.001). Possible non-union in 4 patients (2.6%) at 6 weeks.

PMID:23725485.other_findings: Residents operated in 65 minutes versus 45 minutes for attending surgeons, with no significant radiographic differences. No hardware failure or wound complications.

PMID:41049717.topic: Post-operative weight-bearing after hip fracture surgery
PMID:41049717.setting: National Hip Fracture Database aggregate data from 169 hospitals in England, Wales and Northern Ireland
PMID:41049717.standard: NICE hip fracture guideline (2011): early unrestricted weight-bearing after surgery; no target stated

cycle1.result: 93.2% full weight-bearing, 3.1% (2310) non-weight-bearing and 3.6% not recorded. Nine hospitals made 10% or more of cases non-weight-bearing; one site recorded 100% non-weight-bearing.

PMID:41049717.other_findings: Reasons for non-weight-bearing are not recorded by the NHFD. The highlights give the full weight-bearing figure as 93.8%.

PMID:41113895.topic: Marker ball placement on pelvic radiographs
PMID:41113895.setting: Poole General Hospital trauma unit (district general hospital); AP pelvic radiographs for intracapsular neck of femur fractures
PMID:41113895.standard: Local trauma unit guideline: marker ball entirely visible and placed between the femurs inferior to the symphysis pubis; agreed target 80% for each

cycle1.result: Marker ball present in 27 (45%). Of these, entirely visible 16 (59%) and correctly positioned 11 (41%); overall compliance 59% (n=16).

PMID:41113895.intervention: Poster reminders in radiography areas, a presentation to the radiography team by a T&O registrar, and a mandatory checklist for all such X-rays.

cycle2.result: Marker ball present in 39 (78%). Entirely visible 33 (84%, p=0.042) and correctly positioned 32 (82%, p=0.0014); overall compliance 80% (n=31, p=0.132), meeting the target.

PMID:41113895.other_findings: The methods state the first cycle was completed in June 2025, overlapping the re-audit dates given in the abstract. No inter-observer reliability testing was done.

PMID:34926032.setting: Galway University Hospitals, tertiary referral centre; consent forms for emergency orthopaedic trauma surgery
PMID:34926032.standard: American Association of Orthopaedic Surgeons 'Orthopaedic Surgical Consent' standards (name, DOB, board number, procedure without abbreviation, side/site stated); no target stated

cycle1.result: Name, DOB and board number 100%. No abbreviations 79 (74.5%). Side/site 81 (76.4%) (the abstract wording says 'without correctly stating' but the comparison treats this as compliance). Abbreviation and side/site both failing in 13 (12.3%).

PMID:34926032.intervention: A single 90-minute virtual education session for all trauma and orthopaedic staff on consent standards, sharing cycle 1 results.

cycle2.result: Name, DOB and board number 100%. No abbreviations 37 (92.5%, p=0.02). Side/site correctly stated 39 (97.5%, p=0.0015). No form had both failures (0% vs 12.3%, p=0.02).

PMID:34926032.other_findings: Only 106 of 147 and 40 of 57 consent forms were available for review. The abstract gives the cycle 1 sample as 107.

PMID:26800621.setting: Vancouver General Hospital, acute hospital; patients coded as subtrochanteric femoral fractures
PMID:26800621.standard: Published diagnostic criteria for atypical femoral fracture; no target stated

cycle1.result: Of 204 patients coded as subtrochanteric fractures, 178 had radiographic evidence of other fracture types. Of 193 with radiographs reviewed, 24 (12.4%) met AFF criteria; radiologists had diagnosed AFF in only 1 of the 24.

PMID:26800621.other_findings: 75% of AFF patients were on bisphosphonates. 12 of 19 (63%) with contralateral femur imaging had a contralateral focus of periosteal/endosteal new bone.

PMID:21134142.setting: Orthopaedics, Kent and Sussex Hospital, Tunbridge Wells; foundation-year doctors starting orthopaedic posts
PMID:21134142.standard: Orthopaedic consultants' expectations of basic knowledge, assessed by a test; no target stated

cycle1.result: Knowledge was inadequate against consultants' basic expectations (no figures in abstract).

PMID:21134142.intervention: A focused 2-week teaching programme at the start of the orthopaedic job.

cycle2.result: Standards improved significantly on a different retest (no figures in abstract).

PMID:21134142.other_findings: Junior doctors' confidence and enjoyment of the specialty also increased. Only the abstract was available.
